newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy June fund inflow seen good, Italy equity less.
newsitem.headline: Italy June fund inflow seen good, Italy equity less.

text.p: Inflows into Italian mutual funds are expected to continue at healthy levels in June but domestic equity funds are seen again being neglected in favour of foreign stock funds, fund managers polled by Reuters said on Wednesday.
Managers noted that despite the robust performance of the Milan stock market, Italian equity funds were being left behind in terms of inflows.
The all-share Mibtel index has risen some 30 percent since the start of the year, setting a new high of 13,541 Wednesday.

But equity analysts noted that the authoritative BCI (Comit) index, while posting a 27 percent gain so far this year, was well below its May 1986 record high of 908.20. The index, fixed each day after the bourse close, was at 839.27 on Tuesday.

Italian investors, while traditionally favouring bond and money market funds, have nevertheless turned away from domestic equity funds in a major way this year, placing about three times more in international stock funds, fund managers said.
Falling yields on Italian government bonds have also played a big part in encouraging savers to look elsewhere for good returns, they said.
Data for May from industry body Assogestioni showed net inflows into foreign equity funds totalled 1.36 trillion lire while domestic funds showed a new outflow of 187 billion lire.
Total net inflows into Italian mutual funds in May were 5.709 trillion lire, up on 4.964 trillion lire in April.
Assogestioni data for June are due out towards the end of next week.
As for individual fund managers, Gesticredit estimated it would have a June overall inflow of 800 to 900 billion lire against 1.19 trillion lire in May.

A Gesticredit official said equity funds represented 19.3 percent of the total against 12 percent in May, with bond funds some 65 percent, slightly down on May. Italian equity funds were seen posting zero growth in line with May.
San Paolo saw inflows, of 500 billion lire in mid-June, in line with May's total 900 billion lire, with an increasing diversification towards international equity products.
Centrale Fondi said it had inflows on June 20 of 600 billion lire against 493 billion in May, while GenerComit expected inflows "considerably higher" than the 483 billion lire of May.

"The move towards equity funds is continuing," said Francesco Taranto, managing director of Prime Merrill Funds. "But I don't think there is any longer a direct link between the Milan bourse's performance and fund inflows. Investors are looking for good opportunities in terms of diversification."

Attilio Ferrari, managing director of Arca Fondi, noted that "current redemptions by subscribers who came in the last time the Milan Mibtel index was at highs in early 1994 are preventing Italian equity funds from growing in a decisive way."

Gianluigi Costanzo, director-general of Caboto Gestioni, also pointed to the lack of savings going into domestic share funds. "Perhaps share placements like those of San Paolo Bank or energy group ENI have an influence but it's a fairly surprising phenomenon when you think that those who subscribed to an equity fund at the beginning of this year have already seen yields well above those of bond funds," he said.
